scenes.text: It's 1873, and Wall Street is collapsing in a panic.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Wall Street outside a bank during the 1873 panic: granite columns, closed iron doors, papers scattered on the cobbles, overcast sky

scenes.text: Panicked men are screaming as banks lock their doors around them.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Wall Street outside a bank during the 1873 panic: granite columns, closed iron doors, papers scattered on the cobbles, overcast sky

scenes.text: And you are one of the few who stays calm.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Wall Street outside a bank during the 1873 panic: granite columns, closed iron doors, papers scattered on the cobbles, overcast sky

scenes.text: Because you're holding the one thing nobody else has: cash.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When you die, you will be the richest woman in America.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And the entire nation will call you the Witch of Wall Street.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: THE WITCH OF WALL STREET DIES

scenes.text: By the end, you'll know the one money rule that got you there, and whether it still works today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But to get there, we have to go back.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It's 1834, and you're born in New Bedford, Massachusetts.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your name is Henrietta Howland Robinson.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That panic is thirty-nine years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: Keep count of the money, the children, and the enemies.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: Your family built a massive fortune selling whale oil.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Because whale oil burns cleanly, everyone pays top dollar for it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your grandfather has failing eyes, so at age six, you read him financial papers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Other kids hear fairy tales, but you learn bond yields: interest paid on debt.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By age eight, you open your very first bank account.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your father is a strict businessman who hates unnecessary spending.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: He wears old clothes until they rot.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: Your mother is constantly sick, so your family sends you to Aunt Sylvia.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Aunt Sylvia is a wealthy Quaker spinster who lives extremely simply.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: She teaches you that wealth is preserved by avoiding wasteful habits.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: She also saves every scrap of paper and reuses old ribbon.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: By age thirteen, you take over the family ledgers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You calculate shipping profits faster than adult clerks.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: At twenty, your father sends you to New York to buy fashionable dresses.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He gives you twelve hundred dollars, which is about forty thousand today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You buy cheap clothes instead and invest the rest in government bonds.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You return home wearing plain cotton.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: Your father is so impressed that he entrusts you with more capital.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: Now let's explain compound interest: the money idea at the heart of your strategy.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: Imagine planting one apple tree in your garden.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: Every year, it drops ten apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: Instead of eating them, you plant the seeds of all ten apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: Soon you have eleven trees dropping one hundred and ten apples.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: You keep planting every single seed, never taking a bite.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: That is compound interest: earning returns on your previous returns.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New England apple orchard, 1850s: rows of apple trees heavy with red apples, wooden ladder, baskets, summer afternoon

scenes.text: The panic that makes you rich is nineteen years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: In 1860, your mother passes away.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: She leaves you an eight thousand dollar house, and the rest goes to your father.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: You are furious at the unequal distribution.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New Bedford whaling merchant's house interior, 1840s: ship paintings, ledgers on a desk, oil lamps, harbor through the window

scenes.text: In 1865, your father dies in New York.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He leaves an estate of about six million dollars: around two hundred million today.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: All but one million goes into a trust that pays you only the interest.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Just two weeks later, Aunt Sylvia dies as well.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You expect her two million dollar estate to come directly to you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Instead, her will leaves half to charity and half in trust.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You produce a second document claiming she wanted you to have everything.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The family accuses you of forging her signature.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: This leads to the famous Howland Will case.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Mathematicians analyze the strokes to argue the signature is traced.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The experts are Benjamin Peirce and his son Charles, famous Harvard mathematicians.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: They compare dozens of your aunt's real signatures, stroke by stroke.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Real signatures never match perfectly, because a hand never moves the same way twice.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But the signature on your page matches another one almost exactly.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Their answer: the odds of that by chance are less than one in a billion trillion.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Benjamin Peirce tells the court: so vast an improbability is practically an impossibility.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: So vast an improbability is practically an impossibility.

scenes.text: It's one of the first times statistics is used as evidence in an American court.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Facing potential forgery charges, you decide to leave the country.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1867, you marry Edward Henry Green, a wealthy silk trader.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Before saying yes, you make him sign a strict prenuptial agreement.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your money stays entirely yours, and his money stays entirely his.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Which is a pretty bold thing to ask of a groom in 1867.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You move to London, away from the lawsuit, and start investing heavy cash.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1868, you give birth to your son, Ned Green.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Back home, the court rules against you in 1868, and the trust stands.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You never get the principal, only the income it pays.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The fight leaves you convinced that everyone is after your money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The American Civil War has left government bonds heavily discounted.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: People think the United States government will collapse and fail to pay.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You buy millions in greenbacks: paper currency issued during the war.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Years later, Congress backs greenbacks with gold, and yours soar in value.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1871, you give birth to your daughter, Sylvia.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The panic that makes you rich is two years away.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1873, the Panic hits Wall Street.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Wall Street outside a bank during the 1873 panic: granite columns, closed iron doors, papers scattered on the cobbles, overcast sky

scenes.text: Railroads go bankrupt and major banking houses fail.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: Wall Street outside a bank during the 1873 panic: granite columns, closed iron doors, papers scattered on the cobbles, overcast sky

scenes.text: While everyone panics, you hold pure liquid cash.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You buy distressed railroad stocks for pennies on the dollar.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When the market recovers, your investments multiply several times over.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: After years in London, your family finally sails home to America.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You move into your mother-in-law's house in Bellows Falls, Vermont.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your children grow up watching you count every penny.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your husband Edward loves grand living, fine cigars, and speculation.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He makes high-risk investments using borrowed money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1885, your bank, John J. Cisco and Son, goes bankrupt.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Edward owes the bank money, and they hold your deposits.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The bank demands you cover his debt.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember that prenuptial agreement?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You pull out the signed contract and fight for every penny.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You move your money to another bank and Edward out of your life.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Which is a pretty harsh end to an eighteen year marriage.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Now let's address the popular rumors about your frugality.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The internet says you let your son lose his leg to avoid paying a doctor.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: It didn't happen.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MYTH: REFUSED ALL DOCTORS FOR NED

scenes.text: You took him to free clinics, but you also hired specialists.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: His leg was amputated years later after a long infection.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The internet also says you never used warm water to save on heating.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: There's no solid evidence it's true.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You lived in cheap boarding houses mainly to avoid tax assessors.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You rent small rooms in Hoboken, New Jersey, across the river from Wall Street.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You sign the lease under fake names, like Mrs. C. Dewey.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Why? New York tax collectors want a share of your fortune.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here is a tax residence: the place that decides which city taxes you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Move often enough, and no city can prove where you live.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You ride the ferry to Manhattan every day, carrying your bag of bonds.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You also carry a revolver, in case anyone tries to rob you.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You carry your papers in a battered black bag and wear one dark dress.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You only wash the bottom hem of the dress to save soap.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember Aunt Sylvia's lessons on avoiding waste?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Press reporters label you the Witch of Wall Street.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: HETTY GREEN: THE WITCH OF WALL STREET

scenes.text: You work from a desk at the Chemical Bank.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cluttered back office of a big New York bank, 1890s: plain desk piled with bonds and papers, radiator, iron safe, frosted glass partition

scenes.text: You eat oatmeal warmed on a radiator instead of buying lunch.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cluttered back office of a big New York bank, 1890s: plain desk piled with bonds and papers, radiator, iron safe, frosted glass partition

scenes.text: Remember your father wearing old clothes until they rotted?
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cluttered back office of a big New York bank, 1890s: plain desk piled with bonds and papers, radiator, iron safe, frosted glass partition

scenes.text: In 1893, another massive financial panic strikes Wall Street.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Major banks run completely out of cash.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here is a bank run: when everyone tries to withdraw cash at once.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Banks keep only a small fraction of deposits in their vault.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When customers panic and line up outside, the cash runs out fast.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The bank closes its doors, leaving depositors broke.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: While banks fail around you, your money sits safely in cash and bonds.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You lend to desperate borrowers, but only against real property.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here is a mortgage: a loan where the borrower pledges land or buildings.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If the borrower can't pay, the lender takes the property.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Over the years, you end up owning large amounts of Chicago real estate.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Panics don't scare you, because you never borrow to invest.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: cluttered back office of a big New York bank, 1890s: plain desk piled with bonds and papers, radiator, iron safe, frosted glass partition

scenes.text: Remember Edward's borrowed money?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: That's exactly what ruined him.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: When railroad lines default, you take control of the actual tracks.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You gain control of a Texas railroad.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You personally inspect the lines to stop wasteful managers.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You send Ned to Texas to run the Texas Midland Railroad.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He's in his twenties, with one leg and a big appetite for spending.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He turns the railroad around and even gets into Texas politics.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1902, your estranged husband Edward falls seriously ill.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Despite the past, you return to nurse him in his final months.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He dies in 1902, and you wear black mourning dress for good.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: The Panic of 1907 brings Wall Street to its knees once again.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Major trust companies fail and stock prices collapse nationwide.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Financier J.P. Morgan scrambles to organize a massive bailout.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Desperate city leaders ask you for another emergency loan.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New York City Hall mayor's office, 1907: dark wood panels, tall windows, city seal on the wall, desk with ledgers

scenes.text: You write a check for one point one million dollars to save the city.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New York City Hall mayor's office, 1907: dark wood panels, tall windows, city seal on the wall, desk with ledgers

scenes.text: In return, you take short-term city revenue bonds.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: New York City Hall mayor's office, 1907: dark wood panels, tall windows, city seal on the wall, desk with ledgers

scenes.text: Of your panic loans you say: those to whom I loaned money got it at six percent.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: Those to whom I loaned money got it at 6%.

scenes.bgIdea: New York City Hall mayor's office, 1907: dark wood panels, tall windows, city seal on the wall, desk with ledgers

scenes.text: Your rule: when I see a good thing going cheap, I buy a lot of it.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: When I see a good thing going cheap, I buy a lot of it.

scenes.bgIdea: New York City Hall mayor's office, 1907: dark wood panels, tall windows, city seal on the wall, desk with ledgers

scenes.text: While rival investors lose everything, your wealth keeps climbing.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your son Ned keeps running your business in Texas.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He spends lavishly and collects expensive automobiles.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In 1909, your daughter Sylvia finally marries, at thirty-eight.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Her groom is Matthew Astor Wilks, from the wealthy Astor family.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Before the wedding, you make him sign away any claim to her fortune.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Remember your own prenuptial agreement?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Your daughter Sylvia lives quietly under your strict financial guidance.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented Manhattan apartment, 1910s: narrow bed, plain dresser, radiator, one window over brick buildings

scenes.text: In 1916, at eighty-one, you argue with a maid over skimmed milk.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented Manhattan apartment, 1910s: narrow bed, plain dresser, radiator, one window over brick buildings

scenes.text: A series of strokes soon ends your life.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You die on July third, 1916, in New York, at eighty-one.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.bgIdea: small rented Manhattan apartment, 1910s: narrow bed, plain dresser, radiator, one window over brick buildings

scenes.text: Your fortune goes to your two children, Ned and Sylvia.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Ned spends his share on yachts, coins, stamps, and a seaside mansion.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: He even buys a whole sheet of the rare Inverted Jenny airmail stamps.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Sylvia dies in 1951 and leaves most of the money to charities and friends.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Decades later, Guinness World Records lists you as the greatest miser.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: So how did a girl from New Bedford become the richest woman in America?
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: You let interest compound, held cash for the panics, and skipped the vanity.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In your own words: all you have to do is buy cheap and sell dear.
scenes.speaker: narrator

quote.text: All you have to do is buy cheap and sell dear.

scenes.text: Your fortune is worth billions in today's money.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Here is the money rule from your life.
scenes.speaker: narrator

paper.text: MONEY RULE: KEEP CASH FOR PANICS

scenes.text: Keep some cash ready, so a crash becomes a sale instead of a disaster.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: In early 2020, stocks fell about a third in one month.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If you had to sell then, you locked in that loss.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: If you had cash waiting, you bought the same things at a discount.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: But idle cash loses value to inflation every single year.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: And your way cost you comfort, family warmth, and almost every friend.
scenes.speaker: narrator

scenes.text: Buy when everyone sells, hold cash, and never pay for an expensive lunch.
scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.title: YOUR LIFE AS HETTY GREEN

meta.thumbnail: Hetty Green in a plain black dress clutching a bag of cash while a bank crowd panics behind her; text: 'WITCH OF WALL STREET'.
meta.description:
It's 1834, and you're born into a whaling fortune in New Bedford. Decades later, you hold the cash when Wall Street panics.

A comedic dramatization of documented history. Some well-known anecdotes about her thrift are disputed.

Sources:
- Hetty Green, Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hetty_Green
- Fortune, how the richest woman in the world helped save New York City in the Panic of 1907: https://fortune.com/2024/03/17/how-richest-woman-world-saved-new-york-city-panic-1907/
- Vermont Historical Society, Henrietta Howland Robinson Green: https://hub.catalogit.app/vermont-historical-society/folder/entry/89dd1eb0-a79f-11ea-8dbd-dd0b3b7e0130
Further reading:
- Janet Wallach, The Richest Woman in America (2012)
